text:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] rate-limiter-service: abnormal surge in 429s and error budget consumption in eu-west-1 detected at 2026-03-15T03:10:34Z. Paging oncall @maria-oncall :rotating_light:

maria-oncall: seeing spike on the dashboard now. 429s from several enterprise tenants starting ~03:08. I'm on it.

nate-eng: I can help. Any recent deploys or flag changes?

maria-oncall: small canary rollout for `rlv2-ratecap` at 03:05 — there was a config push touching exemptions and penalty-buckets.

kevin-sre: infra notes: change deployed via k8s configmap `rlv2-config` and a feature-flag `ratecap_v2` enabled for canary group only.

lisa-support: getting inbound tickets — acct-42, acct-178, acct-enterpriseX report throttling/failed requests. ETA on root cause? Customers are asking.

ops-bot: Created incident channel #incidents/1966001234 and assigned severity: Sev2 (partial enterprise impact).

nate-eng: canary logs show repeated messages: ``[WARN] request rejected: exemptions not found for tenant=acct-42; decision=throttle``

maria-oncall: that suggests exemptions key may have been overwritten or dropped during the config merge.

alex-product: need immediate mitigation — can we stop the rollout and flip the flag off for canary? Also prepare a short customer notice.

kevin-sre: flipping `ratecap_v2` back to OFF for canary now. Using: ``/ops feature-flag flip ratecap_v2 --env=prod --group=canary --value=false``

incidents-bot: Feature flag flip initiated by kevin-sre.

kevin-sre: flip complete. Confirming canary nodes show flag=false. 429 rate improving but some sessions still exhibiting 429s.

nate-eng: I'll roll back the configmap to the prior revision on canary and pause any additional rollouts. Commands:

```
kubectl -n prod set data configmap rlv2-config --from-file=rlv2-config.yaml=@/releases/rlv2-config-v11.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deployment/rate-limiter-canary -n prod
```

maria-oncall: rollback started. Pods restarting; expected convergence ~40s.

incidents-bot: Rollback started at 03:16:00Z by nate-eng.

lisa-support: drafting customer message: short note + followup RCA. Please review: "We observed a configuration rollout that unintentionally removed exemption entries for a subset of enterprise tenants, causing transient 429 responses. We paused the rollout and reverted the configuration; services have returned to normal."

alex-product: language looks good. Keep it concise and avoid technical jargon.

kevin-sre: pods back up. Canary 429 rate dropped from 6.8% to 0.6% within 90s post-rollback.

nate-eng: while triaging, noticed token accounting warnings: ``token_accounting: negative_delta tenant=acct-178`` — looks like an aggregator race condition. Adding to follow-up list.

maria-oncall: main mitigation (flag off + rollback) worked. We'll keep incident open for RCA and verify no other clusters affected.

lisa-support: customers are seeing recovery. acct-enterpriseX requested exact timestamps and affected endpoints.

customer-ops: confirming customers want a timeline and mitigation steps. Recommend noting best-effort retries worked and to restart any long-running requests after 03:16 UTC.

nate-eng: impact window recorded: 03:08 -> 03:16 UTC. I'll log this in the incident record.

kevin-sre: preliminary hypothesis: a config merge script performed a shallow merge and replaced `exemptions` with an empty array when updating schema. That'd explain canary-only missing exemptions.

incidents-bot: Task created: "Add CI validation to ensure exemptions present and prevent shallow merges" assigned to nate-eng and kevin-sre.

maria-oncall: immediate action items: 1) confirm other regions/clusters have correct exemptions 2) reproduce shallow-merge locally 3) investigate token-accounting negative_delta 4) finalize customer comms. I'll hand off to next oncall @pager-duty in ~10m.

pager-duty: acknowledged. I will continue monitoring eu-west-1 and coordinate RCA follow-up.

nate-eng: token-accounting negative_delta appears to be a reporting artifact from concurrent ledger updates in the aggregator. No evidence of actual token loss. I'll compare raw event stream to aggregator state to confirm.

customer-ops: customer asks for ETA on RCA. Recommend sending preliminary RCA within 24 hours and full postmortem within 3 business days.

lisa-support: sending preliminary note to impacted customers marking issue as mitigated and promising follow-up.

incidents-bot: Incident state: Mitigated (rollback + flag flip). Owner: nate-eng. Please update tasks and assign follow-ups in the incident tracker.

maria-oncall: final — great job everyone. Please add any remaining follow-ups and owners. I'll review the RCA draft with product in the morning. :white_check_mark:
